bullet_points: Download 200 evenly spaced VTK snapshots (every 5th snapshot: 18903, 18908, ..., 19898) from the HuggingFace dataset.
Use the URL template: `https://huggingface.co/datasets/pedrota2000/NS_simulation/resolve/main/Turb.hydro_w.NNNNN.vtk`
Save the files to `{database_path}`.
Skip downloading if the file already exists and has a size > 0.
Print the number of successfully downloaded files.
Implement a streaming loader that reads the 200 downloaded VTK snapshots sequentially.
For each snapshot, compute the Q-criterion field using central finite differences with periodic boundary wrapping.
Perform a 3D FFT on the velocity grid to extract the large-scale solenoidal driving component (wavenumbers 1 <= n <= 3) and inverse FFT to get `V_LS`.
Compute and cache the Q-criterion and `V_LS` fields to disk (or memory if manageable) before starting the tracer integration to ensure modularity and recoverability.
Initialize 5,000 standard tracers at random positions in the domain [-0.5, 0.5]^3.
Select the first 1,000 of these as base tracers for FTLE. For each, initialize 3 perturbed neighbors offset by `delta = 0.01 * dx` in the x, y, and z directions. Total tracers = 8,000.
Integrate all 8,000 tracers using an RK4 scheme with 10 sub-steps per snapshot interval (dt = 0.01 / 10).

Use `scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator` for spatial interpolation of the full velocity and `V_LS`. You must use vectorized batch interpolation (passing all tracer positions at once) with the `method='linear'` for speed. Construct the interpolators once per snapshot and reuse them across all sub-steps within that interval.
Enforce periodic boundary conditions via modulo arithmetic at each sub-step.
Interpolate and store the full velocity `V`, large-scale velocity `V_LS`, and Q-criterion at the positions of the 5,000 standard tracers at each snapshot.
Save a 2D slice (e.g., z=0) of the Q-criterion and velocity field from the final snapshot for visualization.
Save the wrapped trajectories of all 8,000 tracers, and the interpolated `V`, `V_LS`, and Q-criterion data to `.npy` or `.npz` files in `{database_path}`.
Load the wrapped trajectories of the 8,000 tracers from `{database_path}`.
The first 1,000 are the base tracers, and the remaining 3,000 are their perturbed neighbors (1,000 for x-offset, 1,000 for y-offset, 1,000 for z-offset).

For each of the 1,000 base tracers, compute the flow map gradient (Jacobian matrix F) at each time step using the finite differences between the base tracer and its 3 perturbed neighbors. Note that this one-sided finite difference approximation is acceptable.
Print the mean initial separation magnitude to verify the numerical appropriateness of the perturbation size.
Crucial: Use the minimum image convention to compute the separation vectors to correctly handle periodic boundary crossings.
Compute the Cauchy-Green deformation tensor `C = F^T F` and extract the maximum eigenvalue `lambda_max`.
Calculate the FTLE over time: `FTLE(t) = (1 / (2 * t)) * ln(lambda_max)`. (Handle t=0 appropriately to avoid division by zero).
Save the computed FTLE values for the 1,000 tracers to a `.npy` file in `{database_path}`.
Load the wrapped trajectories and full velocity `V` of the 5,000 standard tracers.
Compute the ensemble-averaged Mean-Square Displacement MSD(t) and component-wise MSD_x, MSD_y, MSD_z using the minimum image convention for displacements.
Calculate the Velocity Autocorrelation Function (VACF) using the stored full velocities `V` and integrate it to find the Lagrangian Integral Time Scale (tau_L).
Print the final VACF value and note whether the integral has converged. Use only the positive lobe of the VACF for the tau_L estimation if the function fails to decay to zero.
Compute the time-dependent power-law exponent alpha(t) = d(log MSD) / d(log t) using numerical differentiation.
Save MSD(t), component MSDs, VACF, tau_L, and alpha(t) to a `.npz` file in `{database_path}`.
Load the wrapped trajectories and the interpolated large-scale velocity vectors (`V_LS`) for the 5,000 standard tracers.
At each time step, compute the displacement vector `d(t) = x(t) - x(0)` using the minimum image convention.
Project `d(t)` onto the instantaneous local large-scale velocity vector `V_LS(x(t), t)` to get the parallel displacement component. Note that this Lagrangian frame decomposition is intentional.
Print the mean magnitude of `V_LS` to confirm it is non-negligible.
Compute the perpendicular displacement squared: `d_perp^2 = ||d||^2 - d_parallel^2`.
Calculate the ensemble-averaged MSD_parallel(t) and MSD_perp(t).
Compute the dynamic anisotropy ratio lambda(t) = MSD_parallel(t) / MSD_perp(t).
Save MSD_parallel, MSD_perp, and lambda(t) to a `.npz` file in `{database_path}`.
Load the Q-criterion values along the trajectories of the 5,000 standard tracers, and the FTLE data for the first 1,000 tracers.
Define a threshold `Q_threshold = mean(Q) + std(Q)` computed from the full 3D Q-criterion field at the initial snapshot.
Print the threshold value and the fraction of tracer-time samples exceeding it.
Identify "Trapped" cohorts as tracers residing in regions with `Q > Q_threshold`.
Track entry and exit times to identify full trapping events and compute the residence time for each event.
For the 1,000 tracers with FTLE data, correlate their residence time in vortices with the local FTLE values at the exact point of exit.
Save the trapping events, residence times, and the correlation data (residence time vs exit FTLE) to a `.npz` file in `{database_path}`.
Load the wrapped trajectories of the 5,000 standard tracers and the computed `tau_L`.
Compute the probability density functions (PDFs) of 1D tracer displacements (e.g., x-component, using minimum image convention) at multiple time intervals (e.g., t = 0.5 tau_L, 1.0 tau_L, 2.0 tau_L).
Use Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) or a robust curve fitting method to fit power-law tails to the displacement distributions and estimate the Levy stability index alpha_L.
Perform a Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test against a Gaussian distribution for these time intervals to quantify non-Gaussianity.
Compute and save the kurtosis excess of displacement distributions to complement the KS test for tail analysis.
Save the PDFs, fitted alpha_L values, KS test statistics, and kurtosis excess to a `.npz` file in `{database_path}`.
Load all the computed metrics from previous steps.
Group all plots into a maximum of three multi-panel figures to improve readability and reduce output file count.

Figure 1 (Scaling and Anisotropy): MSD(t) and component-wise MSDs with theoretical geometric saturation limit (L^2/6); Time-dependent power-law exponent alpha(t) vs time; Dynamic anisotropy ratio lambda(t) vs time.

Figure 2 (Distributions and Spatial): Displacement PDFs at the selected time intervals with fitted power-law tails and Gaussian references; 2D spatial visualization of tracer density overlaid with Q-criterion contours.
Figure 3 (Trapping Dynamics): Scatter plot of residence time vs. local FTLE at exit, with a trendline.
Save all figures as high-resolution PNGs in `{database_path}`.
Review all the printed statistics, KS test results, Levy stability indices, kurtosis excess, and descriptions of the generated plots.
Write the full Results section of the paper.
Discuss the ballistic-to-superdiffusive crossover, the impact of solenoidal driving on anisotropy (lambda), the geometric saturation, and the evidence of Levy flights vs sweeping-induced heavy tails.
Explicitly address whether the V_LS decomposition and displacement PDFs are sufficient to distinguish between Levy flights and sweeping-induced heavy tails, noting any limitations.
Interpret the correlation between vortex residence times and FTLE at ejection.
